question: In 10 years A will be twice as old as B was 10 years ago. If A is 9 years older than B, then the present age of A is:
solution:
Given:

In 10 years, A will be twice as old as B was 10 years ago.

A is 9 years older than B

Calculation:

Let the present age of A and B be 'A' and 'B' years respectively

⇒ A = B + 9

Age of A in 10 years will be (A + 10) years

Age of B, 10 years ago = (B – 10) years

A + 10 = 2 × (B – 10)

⇒ A = 2B – 20 – 10

⇒ A = 2B – 30

By equating the value of A, we'll get

B + 9 = 2B – 30

⇒ B = 39

⇒ A = B + 9

⇒ A = 39 + 9 = 48 

∴ Present age of A is 48 years

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**
